correctness.rationale: A legal profile consists of a downset L below the new point and an upset U above it with every member of L strictly below every member of U; this is necessary and sufficient for transitivity without new comparisons on the parameters. Fraïssé extension realizes every profile; homogeneity fixes its complete type over named parameters, and any finite number of mutually incomparable copies realize the same profile, so the type is nonalgebraic. One independent count splits profiles with an empty side, giving 2D−1 since ideals and filters are in bijection by complement. If both sides are nonempty, choosing u in U shows L is contained in the strict ancestor chain of u. Its greatest element v determines L uniquely as the principal ideal of v. Then U is any nonempty filter of the strict descendant forest of v (automatically a filter in P); its count is the number of ideals of that forest minus one, namely product of the child d-values minus one = d_v−2. The standard empty-or-containing-root split gives d_v and product over components gives D. Thus the sum is exactly 2D+sum d_v−2n−1. This includes the empty case D=1 and t=1. Substitution gives the chain, star and antichain expressions. One postorder pass multiplies once per child and per component and sums once per vertex; every counted integer has O(n) bits, so polynomial bit complexity follows, not linear bit complexity. This is an analytic replay for all sizes. The supplied direct-transitivity checker and its 874-encoding and 24-example recorded output were inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The proof needs ancestor orientation; arbitrary orientations of acyclic cover graphs are outside this formula.
The finite forest test counts encodings, not 874 pairwise nonisomorphic forests, and is not the all-size proof.

evidence: Let a_v be the prior lower recurrence minus 1; on an outward-rooted tree a_v is depth(v)+1. Its upper recurrence U_v is d_v. The prior correction terms combine to sum_v [a_v(U_v−1)−1−sum_{v→w}a_v(U_w−1)]. Telescoping gives sum_v (U_v−2), since a_root=1 and a_v−a_parent=1, yielding the exact frozen scalars on a tree.

For any forest P adjoin a single minimum z below its roots to form a rooted tree Q. The ideal count of Q is D+1, and d_z=D+1. There are t(P) profiles with x>z, D profiles with x incomparable to z (empty lower side in P, arbitrary filter), and one with x<z. Hence t(Q)=t(P)+D+1; substituting into the specialized prior tree formula gives exactly t(P)=2D+sum_v d_v−2n−1, including the empty forest.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The only algebraic simplification is cancellation along parent edges plus the elementary added-minimum identity. This recovers the stated count and one-subtree-scalar O(n) evaluation, not just an alternative higher-cost solution for some instances.
